project.name: URL Shortener
project.summary: A Laravel link shortener: signed-in users create and manage short links over an API, and anyone can open a short code and get sent to the original URL. Redis speeds up those public redirects; MySQL holds the lasting data.

nodes.label: API
nodes.summary: JSON endpoints for signing in and managing short links with a personal token.

nodes.label: Sign-in
nodes.summary: Logs users in, returns a Sanctum token, and answers who is signed in.

nodes.label: Link management
nodes.summary: Create, list, update, and delete short links for the signed-in owner.

nodes.label: Public redirect
nodes.summary: Turns a short code in the browser into a fast jump to the original URL.

nodes.label: Core logic
nodes.summary: The rules and steps for creating, resolving, updating, and authorizing links.

nodes.label: Actions
nodes.summary: One-job steps: create, update, resolve a link, and record a click.

nodes.label: Rules & access
nodes.summary: Checks that URLs are safe, aliases are free, and only owners or admins change links.

nodes.summary: Tables and Eloquent models for users, links, and clicks.

nodes.summary: PHP objects that map to users, short links, and click rows.

links.desc: Controllers call CreateLink and UpdateLink to change data.
The public redirect asks ResolveLink for the destination.
LinkCache stores a small payload per short code in Redis.
Eloquent models persist users, links, and clicks in MySQL.
Only the owner or an admin may change a link.
k6 hits the public redirect to measure latency.

flows.title: Create a short link
flows.description: A signed-in user turns a long URL into a short code.

steps.note: User signs in and gets a personal API token
POST /api/links sends the long URL (and optional alias)
Validation checks the URL is safe and the alias is free
CreateLink picks a unique short code and saves the link
The new link row is stored for later lookups

flows.title: Follow a short link
flows.description: Anyone opens a short code and lands on the original site.

steps.note: LinkCache tries Redis first, then the database
A cache hit avoids a database round-trip
Visitor is sent to the original URL (or 404/410 if gone)
